title: A communicator who treats an institution's pending procedure as a completed decision manufactures certainty the institution has not produced
body:
- A claim confuses a scheduled hearing with an issued order, presenting the institution's future consideration as a decision it has already made.
- The error converts a procedure that has not yet produced an outcome into a narrative that asserts the outcome as completed.
- The misstep hinges on collapsing the temporal distinction between "will consider" and "has ordered."
- The collapsed framing circulates as misinformation because an asserted ruling carries more apparent force than notice that a hearing is scheduled.
- Because the institution has not actually acted, the claim supplies a certainty the source cannot back.
- Case: A claim that a judge had ordered a halt to White House renovation misrepresented an upcoming preliminary-injunction hearing as an injunction already in force.
conversion: a pending procedure becomes a completed decision, manufacturing certainty the institution has not produced
